label: Military power
summary: Whether the character's military power is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`, for example `military_power > 1000`. The game's description does not say how the power is worked out.

label: Appointment level needed
summary: Whether the amount of currency level a title requires for appointments is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Works on a title. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. Vanilla uses it once, as `> 0`.

label: Appointment minimum tier
summary: Whether the lowest title tier at which the ruler's government allows appointment investment is above, below or equal to a tier.
details: Works on a character. Compare it with a tier name such as `tier_county`, for example `min_appointment_tier > tier_county`. Vanilla uses it twice, both times with `tier_county`.

label: Title men-at-arms minimum tier
summary: Whether the lowest title tier that can have a title men-at-arms (MaA) regiment is above, below or equal to a tier.
details: Works on a character. Compare it with a tier name such as `tier_county`, for example `min_title_maa_tier > tier_county`.

label: Birth month
summary: Whether the month of the year in which the character was born matches a number from 1 to 12.
details: 1 is January and 12 is December. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`, for example `month_of_year_of_birth = 12`.

label: Monthly gold balance
summary: Whether the character's monthly gold balance is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. The game does not say how the balance is worked out. For the income and expense parts on their own, see `monthly_character_income` and `monthly_character_expenses`.

label: Monthly expenses
summary: Whether the character's monthly expenses are above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. Vanilla uses it once, comparing against the monthly income (`> monthly_character_income`).

label: Monthly income
summary: Whether the character's monthly income is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. Vanilla uses it a lot, mostly against a script value such as the court position task cost, against the monthly expenses, or against 0.

label: Long-term gold allocated
summary: A gold check tied to the AI's long-term spending category; the game documents it only as a question about allocating gold.
details: The game's text asks "did the character allocate the required gold?" for the AI category long term, yet it accepts number comparisons like the other income checks. What the number means is not documented, and the input shows no vanilla use.

label: Reserved gold allocated
summary: A gold check tied to the AI's reserved spending category; the game documents it only as a question about allocating gold.
details: The game's text asks "did the character allocate the required gold?" for the AI category reserved, yet it accepts number comparisons like the other income checks. What the number means is not documented, and the input shows no vanilla use.

label: Short-term gold allocated
summary: A gold check tied to the AI's short-term spending category; the game documents it only as a question about allocating gold.
details: The game's text asks "did the character allocate the required gold?" for the AI category short term, yet it accepts number comparisons like the other income checks. What the number means is not documented, and the input shows no vanilla use.

label: War chest gold allocated
summary: A gold check tied to the AI's war chest spending category; the game documents it only as a question about allocating gold.
details: The game's text asks "did the character allocate the required gold?" for the AI category war chest, yet it accepts number comparisons like the other income checks. What the number means is not documented, and the input shows no vanilla use.

label: Men-at-arms gold expense
summary: Whether the character's monthly gold cost for military (men-at-arms regiments that are not raised) is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. Only the upkeep of regiments that are not currently raised is counted, according to the game's note.

label: Men-at-arms prestige expense
summary: Whether the character's monthly prestige cost for military (men-at-arms regiments that are not raised) is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. Only the upkeep of regiments that are not currently raised is counted, according to the game's note.

label: Men-at-arms treasury expense
summary: Whether the character's monthly treasury cost for military (men-at-arms regiments that are not raised) is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. Only the upkeep of regiments that are not currently raised is counted, according to the game's note.

label: Monthly treasury balance
summary: Whether the character's monthly treasury balance is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. The number can be negative. Vanilla uses it with `< -50` and `<= 0`.

label: Monthly treasury income
summary: Whether the character's monthly treasury income is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`. Vanilla mostly compares it with the court position task cost, and a few times with fixed numbers from 20 to 60.

label: Long-term treasury allocated
summary: A treasury check tied to the AI's long-term spending category; the game documents it only as a question about allocating treasury.
details: The game's text asks "did the character allocate the required treasury?" for the AI category long term, yet it accepts number comparisons like the other treasury checks. What the number means is not documented, and the input shows no vanilla use.

label: Reserved treasury allocated
summary: A treasury check tied to the AI's reserved spending category; the game documents it only as a question about allocating treasury.
details: The game's text asks "did the character allocate the required treasury?" for the AI category reserved, yet it accepts number comparisons like the other treasury checks. What the number means is not documented, and the input shows no vanilla use.

label: Short-term treasury allocated
summary: A treasury check tied to the AI's short-term spending category; the game documents it only as a question about allocating treasury.
details: The game's text asks "did the character allocate the required treasury?" for the AI category short term, yet it accepts number comparisons like the other treasury checks. What the number means is not documented, and the input shows no vanilla use.

label: War chest treasury allocated
summary: A treasury check tied to the AI's war chest spending category; the game documents it only as a question about allocating treasury.
details: The game's text asks "did the character allocate the required treasury?" for the AI category war chest, yet it accepts number comparisons like the other treasury checks. What the number means is not documented, and the input shows no vanilla use.

label: Treasury income after development
summary: Whether the character's monthly treasury income, after subtracting Vassal Development expenses, is above, below or equal to a number.

label: Monthly control change
summary: Whether the county's total change in county control per month (gains and losses together) is above, below or equal to a number.
details: County control is how firmly the holder controls the county. A positive number means it is growing overall, a negative one that it is shrinking. Works on a county title. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Monthly control decline
summary: Whether the amount of county control the county loses each month, ignoring any growth, is above, below or equal to a number.
details: County control is how firmly the holder controls the county. Works on a county title. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Control decline multiplier
summary: Whether the multiplier applied to the county's control decline rate is above, below or equal to a number.
details: A multiplier of 1.2 means the decline is 20% faster, for example with a single +20% modifier. Works on a county title. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Monthly control growth
summary: Whether the amount of county control the county gains each month, ignoring any decline, is above, below or equal to a number.
details: County control is how firmly the holder controls the county. Works on a county title. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Control growth multiplier
summary: Whether the multiplier applied to the county's control growth rate is above, below or equal to a number.
details: A multiplier of 1.2 means the growth is 20% faster, for example with a single +20% modifier. Works on a county title. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Province monthly income
summary: Whether the monthly income of the province is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Works on a province, not on a character. For a character's income use `monthly_character_income`. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`, for example `monthly_income > 10`.

label: Months as ruler
summary: Whether the number of months the character has been a ruler is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Gives -1 if the character is not a ruler, so a check like `< 5` is also true for non-rulers. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Months since game start
summary: Whether the number of months passed since the start of the game is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Needs no scope; it counts for the whole game. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`, for example `months_from_game_start > 5`. Vanilla uses it often, mostly as `>=` against small fixed numbers such as 1, 8 or 20.

label: Months until max discontent
summary: Whether the number of months until the faction's discontent reaches its maximum of 100 is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Works on a faction. Vanilla uses it with `<= 4`, `<= 8` and `<= 12`. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Gene attribute value
summary: Whether one attribute of a gene of the character's look (for example body height) is above, below or equal to a number.
details: It can only be used in specific places, because it is an interface trigger. Vanilla uses it once, with `value < -0.26` on the height. The example in the game's documentation uses a positive number, so values can be on both sides of zero.

fields.name: category
fields.text: The gene group to look at.
fields.values: a gene category, such as gene_height

fields.name: attribute
fields.values: an attribute name, such as body_height

fields.name: value
fields.text: The comparison for the attribute's value.

label: Gene value
summary: Whether the value of a gene of the character's look (for example baldness) is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Written as `morph_gene_value:gene_baldness > 0.05`, or with the number first. Trait effects on the look are not counted. It can only be used in specific places, because it is an interface trigger. The game's own example also shows a block using `morph_gene_attribute` (a different trigger) next to the `morph_gene_value:` form.

label: Nomad legacy perks
summary: Whether the number of perks the dynasty has in the lifestyle legacy track is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Works on a dynasty. The game's documentation does not say which lifestyle it means; the name points to the nomad (MPO) legacy track. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Not all of
summary: Whether not all of the conditions inside are true.
details: The opposite of `AND`: it is true unless every condition inside is true. It takes a block of triggers.

label: New clerical region size
summary: Whether the size a new clerical region would get, if one were created in this province, is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Works on a province. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`, for example `new_clerical_region_size > 0`.

label: Next arrival date
summary: Whether the estimated date of arrival at the next destination of the travel is before, after or on a given date.
details: Works on a travel plan. Only `<`, `<=`, `=`, `>` and `>=` are possible, not `!=`. The right side must be a valid date.

label: Days to next arrival
summary: Whether the estimated number of days until the travel arrives at its next destination is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Works on a travel plan. Compare it with `<`, `<=`, `=`, `!=`, `>` or `>=`.

label: Progress to next stop
summary: Whether the share of the time already passed on the way to the next destination, from 0.0 to 1.0, is above, below or equal to a number.
details: Works on a travel plan. It is measured from the departure from the previous destination. Vanilla uses values such as `> 0.2`, `> 0.5` and `< 0.8`.

label: None of
summary: Whether none of the conditions inside is true.
details: The opposite of `OR`: it is true only if every condition inside is false. It takes a block of triggers. Vanilla uses it for lists of things that must all not apply, such as `this = scope:person_1` together with a variable check.
